findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "do" references sensitive artifacts (password). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

findings.title: Description uses pressure/override language
findings.detail: Description of "read_page" stacks urgency/override words (always, never). Legitimate tool descriptions rarely pressure the model to act or ignore prior guidance.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: find_business, list_actions, inspect_site, do_action, do, read_page · Private data: find_business, list_actions, inspect_site, do_action, do, read_page · Public sink: list_actions, do_action, do · Destructive: do_action.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: find_business, list_actions, inspect_site, do_action, do, read_page · Private data: find_business, list_actions, inspect_site, do_action, do, read_page · Public sink: list_actions, do_action, do · Destructive: do_action

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
